open_points.subject: CLK-002 witness binding
open_points.text: The only bindings are "CLK-001 [witness: verification:service_identity_consumer_uow_client_portal]; CLK-001 [witness: verification:staff_bootstrap_client_portal]"; the CLK-002 Required tests item has no [witness: ...] binding.
open_points.question: Which existing check is bound to CLK-002 and must assert its clock-source exclusivity, reading-count, validity-boundary and non-persistence requirements?
options: Bind CLK-002 to one existing verification check
Bind its wall-clock and elapsed-clock portions to separate existing checks
Declare that no existing check witnesses CLK-002 and prevent the State 2 handoff
open_points.default_guess: Prevent the handoff until an existing check is explicitly bound.

witness.initial: State 2 contains CLK-002 and its Required tests item, but only CLK-001 has witness tags.
events: A State 8 assembler resolves the witness tags exactly as written.
outcomes: The assembler rejects the handoff because CLK-002 has no bound check.
The assembler treats the prose test description as sufficient and assembles without an existing check bound to CLK-002.
witness.observer: The State 8 assembly gate and later implementers relying on its verdict.

open_points.subject: CLK-002 exclusive host-clock reader invariant
open_points.text: "the clock source is the only reader of the host's wall and elapsed clocks" is paired with tests intended to expose another path only "as a value that does not follow the fixed instant".
open_points.question: What Required test demonstrates that no portal code outside the clock source reads a host clock when such a read is discarded or otherwise does not affect a timestamp or validity decision?
options: A structural/static check forbids host-clock APIs outside the clock-source module
Instrumentation makes every host-clock read observable and asserts that only the clock source performs one
Narrow CLK-002 to prohibit only host-clock reads that affect portal behavior
open_points.default_guess: Add a structural check that host-clock APIs occur only in the clock-source backend.

witness.initial: A mutating operation receives a fixed counting clock source and otherwise writes and compares times exactly as A28 requires.
events: The operation reads the injected source once.
A helper in the same operation also calls datetime.utcnow() directly but discards the result.
The operation writes the injected instant and makes all validity decisions from it.
The specified fixed-source behavioral test runs.
outcomes: The test passes because the extra host-clock read changes no observed value, although CLK-002 is false.
An implementation with an additional structural or instrumented check fails because a component other than the clock source read the host clock.
witness.observer: The verification gate and a maintainer auditing compliance with CLK-002.

open_points.subject: Treatment of unreadable advisory data for uninstalled distributions
open_points.text: The normative rule says "entries naming no installed distribution are not judged," while DEP-002's Required test says "unreadable or unmatchable advisory data ... does not start it" without limiting that refusal to entries naming an installed distribution.
open_points.question: Does unreadable or unmatchable data in an OSV entry for a distribution not installed in the image block the deploy, or is that entry ignored?
options: Ignore it because it names no installed distribution
Block because any unreadable or unmatchable advisory data prevents a passing verdict
Block only when the entry can be matched by normalized name to an installed distribution
open_points.default_guess: Ignore entries whose normalized package name does not match an installed distribution; block unreadable matching entries.

witness.initial: The built image contains distributions alpha and beta. The downloaded OSV archive contains no advisory for either, plus an entry for unrelated distribution gamma whose affected range is malformed and cannot be read by PEP 440.
events: The deployment gate enumerates alpha and beta.
It reads the malformed gamma entry while judging the one downloaded archive.
outcomes: The normative rule does not judge gamma and starts the service because no installed distribution is listed as affected.
The Required-test wording treats the unreadable advisory data as a failed verdict and refuses to start the service.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users waiting for the new service instance.

open_points.subject: Completeness of the OSV PyPI export download
open_points.text: The text requires "OSV's PyPI export archive, downloaded whole" and says "a download that is not whole is a check that cannot complete," but gives no condition by which the gate determines that the archive is whole.
open_points.question: What evidence establishes that the downloaded OSV PyPI export is complete rather than a valid, parseable but incomplete copy?
options: Successful completion of the HTTP transfer is sufficient
The received byte count must match authoritative transfer metadata such as Content-Length
The archive must be verified against an authoritative manifest, checksum or inventory
open_points.default_guess: Require successful transfer completion, byte-count agreement when supplied, and successful full archive parsing; otherwise fail the deploy.

witness.initial: The OSV endpoint returns a syntactically valid PyPI export archive containing only a prefix/subset of the expected entries, with no authoritative checksum, manifest or total-entry count available to the gate.
events: The deployment gate downloads the response successfully.
The archive parses without an error.
The gate must decide whether the copy is "whole" before checking the image.
outcomes: An implementer equates a successfully completed, parseable response with the whole archive and permits the deploy if its entries clear the image.
An implementer requires independent completeness evidence, treats the check as unable to complete, and refuses the deploy.
witness.observer: The deployment operator and users of the release.
